entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Anastasius II was the bishop of Rome from November 24, 496, to his death on November 19, 498. He played a crucial role in ending the Acacian schism, but ultimately failed to achieve lasting success.

Born in Rome, Anastasius II was the son of a priest and was deeply involved in Roman politics and church affairs. His efforts to resolve the Acacian schism led to the Laurentian schism after his death.

Anastasius II is also notable for being one of the last popes to have used the title 'pope' as part of their regnal designation, adopting it in 499 with the intention of stressing the unity and authority of the church.

Despite his efforts to bring peace and stability to Rome, Anastasius II's reign was marked by controversy and conflict. His legacy serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by early Christian leaders in navigating the complexities of power, politics, and faith.

In 1996, Pope John Paul II canonized Anastasius II as a saint, recognizing his dedication to the church and his role in shaping its history.
